nodes.label: HLS heal: rewrite a dead segment host to the playlist's own gateway host
nodes.norm_label: hls heal rewrite dead segment host to the playlist's own gateway host
nodes.summary: When an HLS playlist resolves fine but every segment host is dead, the host that served the playlist usually also serves the same segment paths. Rewriting each absolute segment URL to the playlist URL's own host, saving the playlist locally, and playing that file repairs playback without touching the player or the provider's binary.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-29 - ani-cli-indo-playback-fix [ses_f118969a0ffeRaBW3S6qal4B5G].md:L02872] Host pengganti bukan hardcode — diambil dari URL playlist detik itu juga, jadi dipastikan hidup untuk sesi itu.

nodes.label: A Cloudflare-suspended edge CDN kills only the sub stream while the dub stream plays
nodes.norm_label: a cloudflare-suspended edge cdn kills only the sub stream while the dub stream plays
nodes.summary: For One Piece on hianime.at there is a single server, Vidstream-2 (MegaPlay). Its sub (Japanese audio) segments were served from an edge host that 302-redirects to cloudflare-terms-of-service-abuse.com and 404s, while the dub (English audio) segments went to a different, live host and played normally. The symptom reads as a broken subtitle setting; the cause is a provider-side ToS suspension of one edge host.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-29 - ani-cli-indo-playback-fix [ses_f118969a0ffeRaBW3S6qal4B5G].md:L02246] mpv tetap kebuka tapi ffmpeg gagal load segmen pertama (`404 / Failed to open segment`), jadi videonya gak jalan. Ini murni takedown di sisi sumber, bukan salah `user.js`/config kamu.

Re-measured later in the same session, the edge host still lands on the abuse page and ends on 404 — the curl runs with -sL and prints `final=%{http_code} -> %{url_effective}`: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-29 - ani-cli-indo-playback-fix [ses_f118969a0ffeRaBW3S6qal4B5G].md:L06213] final=404 -> https://www.cloudflare-terms-of-service-abuse.com/stream.jpeg

nodes.label: Comparing playlist EXTINF total against subtitle span rules out framerate drift
nodes.norm_label: comparing playlist extinf total against subtitle span rules out framerate drift
nodes.summary: Summing every EXTINF in the media playlist gives the true video duration; comparing it with the subtitle file's last event gives a ratio. A 1.002 ratio excludes a 25 versus 23.976 fps mismatch, which would show as roughly 1.043 or 0.959, so a global --sub-speed correction is the wrong tool and would only move about 3 seconds at the end.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-29 - ani-cli-indo-playback-fix [ses_f118969a0ffeRaBW3S6qal4B5G].md:L03476] The video's total duration (1477.86s) and the subtitle's last event (1474.6s) are almost identical, only a 0.2% difference. That rules out a PAL/framerate mismatch, which would show up as roughly a 4% gap, so the two timelines aren't off by that kind of scaling issue.

[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-29 - ani-cli-indo-playback-fix [ses_f118969a0ffeRaBW3S6qal4B5G].md:L03707] Kalau ini masalah framerate PAL (25 vs 23.976 fps), rasionya harus ~1.043 atau ~0.959. Jadi **ini bukan masalah framerate**, dan `--sub-speed` global cuma bakal mengoreksi ~3 detik di ujung.

nodes.label: ffmpeg's HLS demuxer does not forward the referrer to segment requests
nodes.norm_label: ffmpeg's hls demuxer does not forward the referrer to segment requests
nodes.summary: A local playlist whose segment URLs are absolute is read by ffmpeg under a file-scheme protocol whitelist (file,crypto,data), so https segment requests are refused outright. Adding https to the whitelist gets past that, but every segment then returns 403 because neither -referer nor -headers reaches the child requests, even though fetching one segment directly with the same flags succeeds. mpv's --referrer does propagate, which is why mpv plays the healed playlist and ffmpeg cannot.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-29 - ani-cli-indo-playback-fix [ses_f118969a0ffeRaBW3S6qal4B5G].md:L04138] A single segment fetch succeeds with the referer flag directly, so ffmpeg can reach the gateway when the header is set explicitly. But going through the m3u8 playlist fails with "Error when loading first segment," which points to the HLS demuxer not propagating the referer header down to segment requests, rather than a fundamental access issue.

[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-29 - ani-cli-indo-playback-fix [ses_f118969a0ffeRaBW3S6qal4B5G].md:L04192] Ah, that's the real error—since heal.m3u8 is local, ffmpeg restricts the protocol whitelist to file,crypto,data, which blocks https segment fetches. I need to expand the whitelist to include https, tls, and tcp alongside the local protocols.

[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-29 - ani-cli-indo-playback-fix [ses_f118969a0ffeRaBW3S6qal4B5G].md:L04287] Now I'm getting HTTP 403 on the actual segments even though the single-segment referer test succeeded, which tells me ffmpeg's HLS demuxer isn't forwarding the `-referer` flag to child segment requests. I need to try passing the referer through `-headers` instead, since that's more likely to propagate across the HLS pipeline.

nodes.label: Sub-second mpv HLS stutter is readahead depth, not bandwidth
nodes.norm_label: sub-second mpv hls stutter is readahead depth, not bandwidth
nodes.summary: Four segments were measured at roughly 2 to 3.6 MB/s, about 22x realtime, so the gateway has bandwidth to spare. mpv's default demuxer-readahead-secs is 1, which fetches HLS segments just in time and stalls at each segment boundary; raising cache-secs and demuxer-readahead-secs to prebuffer about 30 seconds is what removes the stutter.
rationale: Measured gateway segment throughput, the evidence for ruling bandwidth out: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-29 - ani-cli-indo-playback-fix [ses_f118969a0ffeRaBW3S6qal4B5G].md:L03113] seg: code=200 size=1116163B time=0.481464s speed=2318288B/s

[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-29 - ani-cli-indo-playback-fix [ses_f118969a0ffeRaBW3S6qal4B5G].md:L03129] Segment downloads are running around 22x realtime speed, so gateway bandwidth clearly isn't causing the stutter—the bottleneck must be somewhere in mpv itself.

nodes.label: Git history cannot prove a runtime cause
nodes.norm_label: git history cannot prove a runtime cause
nodes.summary: The user reported playback working at the first push to a private repo. All four commits in that repo fall inside a 23-minute window on 2026-09-29 and none of them changes video or patch behaviour, the installed wrapper is byte-identical to the repo copy, and the vendored patched ani-cli is byte-identical to the active /usr/local/bin binary. The playback change therefore cannot be attributed to the repo; the plausible cause is upstream, on the provider's side.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-29 - ani-cli-indo-playback-fix [ses_f118969a0ffeRaBW3S6qal4B5G].md:L08055] Jadi "saat pertama push itu works" — yang bisa kupastikan: **setup-nya nggak berubah sejak push pertama.** Patch 5.1.5-nya sama persis, wrapper-nya sama persis, subtitle-nya sama persis. Kalau video dulu jalan sekarang nggak, itu bukan karena repo berubah. Kemungkinan besar waktu itu hianime/MegaPlay masih nunjukin host CDN yang hidup, dan sekarang `pressforyes.online` kena suspend Cloudflare — perubahan di sisi mereka, di luar repo.

nodes.label: Telegram pref storage is a flat per-installation table, so the gate is per-OS-user and not per-Snipset-account

The token lives in a flat per-installation key/value table (database/schema.rs:65-68), so the gate is per OS user, not per Snipset account and not per cloud profile. nodes.label: Clipboard embedding search is gated off, deadline-capped and silently falls back to LIKE with no tests
nodes.norm_label: clipboard embedding search is gated off, deadline-capped and silently falls back to like with no tests
